BlazeSync AI – Multi-Sensor Satellite Fire Harmonization & Analytics

BlazeSync AI is a Python-based satellite fire data harmonization and analytics platform that integrates NASA FIRMS fire observations from MODIS and multiple VIIRS satellites. The project addresses the challenge of differences in satellite sensor observations, including spatial locations, observation times, coverage, and fire-related measurements.

We developed a data processing pipeline that cleans, validates, and standardizes satellite datasets, identifies potential cross-sensor matches using spatial and temporal criteria, and analyzes Fire Radiative Power (FRP), fire intensity, and geographical clusters. An interactive Streamlit dashboard provides fire hotspot maps, sensor comparisons, matching analysis, charts, data tables, and CSV exports.

This project is important because it brings observations from different satellite instruments into a unified analytical workflow, helping users explore possible fire detections, understand sensor differences, and identify geographical fire patterns. BlazeSync AI aims to support more transparent satellite fire monitoring and data-driven environmental analysis.
details:
BlazeSync AI

BlazeSync AI is a multi-sensor satellite fire harmonization and analytics platform designed to process and compare NASA FIRMS fire observations from MODIS and multiple VIIRS satellites. It addresses the challenge of differences in satellite observations, such as geographical locations, observation times, coverage, and reported fire parameters.

The system works through a Python-based data processing pipeline that collects NASA FIRMS CSV datasets, cleans and standardizes the records, and identifies potential matching fire observations using spatial and temporal criteria. It also performs Fire Radiative Power (FRP) analysis, fire intensity assessment, geospatial clustering, and sensor quality evaluation.

The project provides an interactive Streamlit dashboard featuring fire hotspot maps, cross-sensor matching analysis, MODIS vs. VIIRS comparisons, interactive charts, data tables, and CSV exports.

Benefits and Intended Impact: BlazeSync AI helps users explore satellite fire observations in a unified environment, understand differences between satellite sensors, identify possible corresponding detections, and examine geographical fire patterns. It aims to support environmental monitoring, wildfire data analysis, and informed decision-making.

Technologies Used: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn (where used), Streamlit, Plotly, Folium, NASA FIRMS datasets, and Visual Studio Code.

Creativity and Innovation: The creative aspect of BlazeSync AI is its cross-sensor harmonization approach, which brings multiple satellite observations into one analytical workflow instead of examining each sensor independently. Its matching confidence scores, FRP analysis, geospatial clustering, and interactive visualization make complex satellite data easier to explore.

Factors Considered: Our team considered spatial and temporal differences between sensors, data consistency, missing values, observation quality, geographical accuracy, visualization clarity, and the need for transparent and reproducible analysis. The current study area is India.
